text:
anya: Heads-up — I promoted syrinx-int6 to staging canary (10%) this morning and I'm seeing a surprising recall@1 regression on short queries (<=16 tokens), mostly non-English (JA/KO). anyone else notice? :eyes:

ops-bot: deploy complete — syrinx-int6 v2026-03-23-0800 -> staging (canary 10%). dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/staging/models/syrinx/variants/int6

mike: re-ran the short-holdout quick eval locally against the canary. command I used:
```bash
python eval_recall.py --model syrinx-int6 --queries holdout/short_queries.json --k 1 --seed 42
```
output snippet:
```text
Recall@1: 0.64
Baseline (pelican-v2): 0.71
```

nisha: dropping a per-lang breakdown from the same run (small sample but consistent with what you saw):
```text
lang  baseline  syrinx-int6  delta
en    0.72      0.70         -0.02
ja    0.68      0.57         -0.11
ko    0.71      0.60         -0.11
```

raul: that delta pattern smells like quantization sensitivity around layernorm/softmax for short contexts — int6 tends to amplify small embedding shifts for short queries. two quick experiments: 1) try int8 per-channel (int8_pc) quant for syrinx, 2) route short queries to int8 variant and keep int6 for long queries.

anya: can we flip an experiment flag in staging rather than a full redeploy? want to avoid churn.

devex-bot: you can toggle model variants and traffic splits without redeploying. example:
```bash
redwood model set-variant --model syrinx --variant int8_pc --traffic 5 --env staging
```

mike: kicked off int8_pc 5% traffic in staging. running the same eval now (same seed/files).

mike: quick results from int8_pc run:
```text
Recall@1: 0.69
Baseline (pelican-v2): 0.71
delta overall: -0.02
ja delta: -0.03
ko delta: -0.02
```

nisha: nice — int8_pc recovers most of the loss. I'd still run a larger cohort (n=5k short queries stratified by lang) and check embedding cosine shifts + nearest-neighbor churn. also check timing/latency impact of int8_pc.

mike: latency difference looks negligible in staging (+2-5ms p95). running larger eval overnight and will post numbers in morning.

anya: Proposed rollout plan based on today's triage:
- keep syrinx-int6 for long queries (>64 tokens) where cost win matters
- route short queries (<=16 tokens) to syrinx-int8_pc for now
- run 24h canary for int8_pc at 20% traffic and monitor recall@1, churn, and customers flagged by quality monitors
- run full cohort eval and post results to the model-onboard board

raul: agree. also add a regression alert on recall@1 delta > 0.03 for any language and add an eval that specifically measures recall@1 on short Japanese/English/Spanish splits.

anya: I'll open a rollout ticket and attach these commands + metrics. scheduling 30m sync at 10:30 PT to review the overnight eval. thanks all :thumbsup:

mike: noted. will paste full eval logs to the ticket when done.

nisha: added a quick checklist in the ticket: dataset parity check, caching warmup, kv-cache behavior for short queries, and a small synthetic-anchor test for id-flip.

anya: perfect. tagging @sre for observability knobs when we scale int8_pc canary traffic.

ops-bot: note — created ticket RED-3489: "syrinx int6->int8_pc short-query routing & canary" assigned to anya.
